faults.signature: new product line launches with no KB content; kb_lookup returns no confident hit; answers fall through to a generic reply
faults.primary_effect: cohort resolution_rate falls to ~0.3 against a tenant standard above 0.8 — exact figures in observed_effects.F1
faults.aggregate_effect: tenant containment moves ~2pt — invisible without cohorting

faults.signature: tool returns HTTP 200 with an empty payload on ~14% of calls; outcome is recorded 'ok' so every error-rate metric reads flat
faults.primary_effect: same-tool retry within session, then unresolved end
faults.aggregate_effect: tool_error_rate FLAT — the fault is invisible to the obvious metric and only shows in downstream behaviour

faults.signature: prompt v4 makes the agent over-confirm; turns-to-resolve rises ~60% while resolution rate stays flat
faults.primary_effect: median turns ~4 -> ~6 (mean +58%); cost per session roughly +80%; resolution flat — exact figures in observed_effects.F3
faults.aggregate_effect: resolution FLAT — threshold alerting on outcome metrics misses this entirely; only a standard-relative measure sees it

decoys.signature: campaign drives 5.0x branch_locator volume (a trivially contained intent); AGGREGATE containment RISES while every cohort is flat or slightly worse
decoys.correct_reading: not a quality event in either direction — stratify by intent

decoys.signature: flash sale, 4.0x volume; p95 latency doubles and timeouts rise, then self-corrects. Quality is flat throughout
decoys.correct_reading: a reliability event for the platform view, not a quality regression; it self-corrects inside the sustain window

decoys.signature: quality rubric v1 -> v2 is stricter; judged scores drop ~0.6 across BOTH tenants at once. judge_version is stamped on every judged value, so the information needed to refuse the comparison is present in the data
decoys.correct_reading: do not trend judged quality across the boundary; re-score or segment by judge_version

coverage_traps.description: v2 legacy flow traffic emits no tool_call rows at all.
coverage_traps.correct_behaviour: any tool-derived metric must state coverage and exclude v2 traffic from the denominator, not silently include it

coverage_traps.description: custom_dims.customer_ref is near-unique. The catalog declares a cardinality budget; grouping by it is a planner error.
coverage_traps.correct_behaviour: refuse the breakdown, cite the budget

unanswerable_asks.ask: What is our failover rate — how often did a primary model or tool fail and an alternate serve the user instead?
unanswerable_asks.why: no failover mechanism exists, so no failover event is emitted. There is no primary/secondary path to observe.
unanswerable_asks.nearest_proxy: llm_retry events, which are QUALITY retries at a different temperature — they would under-report and read as '0% failover', i.e. as good news

fidelity_traps.ask: How many users gave up out of frustration rather than getting what they wanted and leaving?
fidelity_traps.why: abandonment is observable; the REASON for it is a judgment about meaning and must be a versioned judged signal with a calibration, not inferred from the session end code

fidelity_traps.ask: How often did a tool call fail?
fidelity_traps.why: we executed the call. Answering this with a model is a Rule 1 violation.

F1.kb_top_score_in_cohort: see agent_steps.kb_top_score — sits in the 0.11-0.38 band

discriminating_fields: step.retry_count on a same-tool second call

D3.cause: rubric v1 -> v2, not agent behaviour
